description: An offline-capable AI health platform that protects astronaut physiological, psychological, and operational performance during deep-space missions by combining space-calibrated vitals monitoring, mental health tracking, AR diagnostics, and predictive digital twins.
summary:
To help astronauts take care of their own health during long space missions when doctors on Earth are too far away.
It uses smart software agents to monitor vital health signs, track risks like radiation or bone loss, and give astronauts clear, easy-to-follow guidance.
In deep space, astronauts must be self-reliant; catching health issues early keeps the crew safe and ensures the mission's success.
details:
What does your project do, and how does it work? It is an autonomous health-monitoring software powered by a multi-agent architecture. It gathers astronaut health indicators (like vital signs and radiation exposure metrics), tracks physiological changes over time, and guides crew members through self-evaluations.

What benefits does it have? It empowers astronauts to independently assess and act on their health status without relying on real-time ground control, which is critical during deep-space communication delays.

What is the intended impact? To prevent critical health conditions (such as bone loss, cardiovascular events, or radiation illness) on long-duration space missions, ensuring crew safety and mission success.

What tools did you use? A multi-agent software framework combined with a sleek, professional user interface design featuring structured workflows and clean visual layouts.

What factors did your team consider? We factored in the extreme isolation, communication blackouts, hostile closed environments, and high-stress cognitive loads that astronauts face during deep-space exploration.
